verses.text: Hannah prayed, and said: “My heart exults in Yahweh! My horn is exalted in Yahweh. My mouth is enlarged over my enemies, because I rejoice in your salvation.
There is no one as holy as Yahweh, For there is no one besides you, nor is there any rock like our God.
“Don’t keep talking so exceedingly proudly. Don’t let arrogance come out of your mouth, For Yahweh is a God of knowledge. By him actions are weighed.
“The bows of the mighty men are broken. Those who stumbled are armed with strength.
Those who were full have hired themselves out for bread. Those who were hungry are satisfied. Yes, the barren has borne seven. She who has many children languishes.
“Yahweh kills, and makes alive. He brings down to Sheol,  and brings up.
Yahweh makes poor, and makes rich. He brings low, he also lifts up.

He raises up the poor out of the dust. He lifts up the needy from the dunghill, To make them sit with princes, and inherit the throne of glory. For the pillars of the earth are Yahweh’s. He has set the world on them.
He will keep the feet of his holy ones, but the wicked shall be put to silence in darkness; for no man shall prevail by strength.

Those who strive with Yahweh shall be broken to pieces. He will thunder against them in the sky. “Yahweh will judge the ends of the earth. He will give strength to his king, and exalt the horn of his anointed.”
Elkanah went to Ramah to his house. The child served Yahweh before Eli the priest.
Now the sons of Eli were wicked men. They didn’t know Yahweh.
The custom of the priests with the people was that when anyone offered a sacrifice, the priest’s servant came while the meat was boiling, with a fork of three teeth in his hand;
and he stabbed it into the pan, or kettle, or cauldron, or pot. The priest took all that the fork brought up for himself. So they did in Shiloh to all the Israelites who came there.
Yes, before they burned the fat, the priest’s servant came, and said to the man who sacrificed, “Give meat to roast for the priest; for he will not accept boiled meat from you, but raw.”
If the man said to him, “Let the fat be burned first, and then take as much as your soul desires”; then he would say, “No, but you shall give it to me now; and if not, I will take it by force.”
The sin of the young men was very great before Yahweh; for the men despised the offering of Yahweh.
But Samuel ministered before Yahweh, being a child, clothed with a linen ephod.
Moreover his mother made him a little robe, and brought it to him from year to year, when she came up with her husband to offer the yearly sacrifice.
Eli blessed Elkanah and his wife, and said, “May Yahweh give you offspring  from this woman for the petition which was asked of Yahweh.” Then they went to their own home.
Yahweh visited Hannah, and she conceived, and bore three sons and two daughters. The child Samuel grew before Yahweh.
Now Eli was very old; and he heard all that his sons did to all Israel, and how that they slept with the women who served at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
He said to them, “Why do you do such things? for I hear of your evil dealings from all this people.
No, my sons; for it is no good report that I hear! You make Yahweh’s people disobey.

If one man sins against another, God will judge him; but if a man sins against Yahweh, who will intercede for him?” Notwithstanding, they didn’t listen to the voice of their father, because Yahweh intended to kill them.
The child Samuel grew on, and increased in favor both with Yahweh, and also with men.
A man of God came to Eli, and said to him, “Yahweh says, ‘Did I reveal myself to the house of your father, when they were in Egypt in bondage to Pharaoh’s house?

Didn’t I choose him out of all the tribes of Israel to be my priest, to go up to my altar, to burn incense, to wear an ephod before me? Didn’t I give to the house of your father all the offerings of the children of Israel made by fire?

Why do you  kick at my sacrifice and at my offering, which I have commanded in my habitation, and honor your sons above me, to make yourselves fat with the best of all the offerings of Israel my people?’

“Therefore Yahweh, the God of Israel, says, ‘I said indeed that your house, and the house of your father, should walk before me forever.’ But now Yahweh says, ‘Far be it from me; for those who honor me I will honor, and those who despise me will be lightly esteemed.
Behold,  the days come, that I will cut off your arm, and the arm of your father’s house, that there will not be an old man in your house.
You will see the affliction of my habitation, in all the wealth which I will give Israel; and there shall not be an old man in your house forever.
The man of yours, whom I don’t cut off from my altar, will consume your eyes  and grieve your heart; and all the increase of your house will die in the flower of their age.
“‘This will be the sign to you, that will come on your two sons, on Hophni and Phinehas: in one day they will both die.
I will raise me up a faithful priest, that will do according to that which is in my heart and in my mind. I will build him a sure house; and he will walk before my anointed forever.

It will happen, that everyone who is left in your house will come and bow down to him for a piece of silver and a loaf of bread, and will say, “Please put me into one of the priests’ offices, that I may eat a morsel of bread.”’”

footnotes.content: Hannah's joy breaks open. After years of silence, her mouth speaks what her heart has held—exultation in the God who heard her when no one else did. This is the prayer of a woman who waited long and knows the Lord's name.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Holy stands alone—set apart, matchless. The rock metaphor echoes throughout Scripture: a shelter, immovable, foundation beneath our feet. Hannah recognizes what she has always known: there is no one like this God.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The rebuke comes gently but firmly: pride is hollow before a God of knowledge. Every deed is weighed. Hannah has learned this truth—not through harshness, but through the long school of waiting and prayer.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The mighty are broken; the stumbled are strengthened. God's reversal startles us every time we meet it, yet it runs through all His dealings. The strong in themselves find their strength is nothing; the weak find sufficiency in Him alone.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hannah herself is the living proof. The hungry was she; now satisfied with a son. The woman who once was barren bears children. Full hunger, empty plenty—God's hand moves beneath the surface, answering the prayer of the humble.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Life and death rest in His hand, not as caprice but as sovereign care. Sheol and life are both His domain. We live at His kindness; we pass at His knowing. There is rest in recognizing we are never beyond His reach.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Poverty and riches, lowliness and honor—all flow from one Hand. The Lord lifts up who He will lift up. This is not chance; it is His wisdom and justice working in history. Hannah's own journey is the proof written on her heart.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From dust and dunghill to the seat of princes—the inheritance that transforms. The earth's pillars belong to Him; He has set them firm. Here is the deepest comfort: the One who holds creation also gathers the forgotten poor.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The holy ones are kept; the wicked hushed in darkness. No strength of flesh prevails. The security we seek is not in muscle or clever scheming, but in walking near to the Lord and keeping our feet within His way.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: His thunder breaks the proud; His word strengthens His king. The anointed one receives the horn of exaltation—a crown from God's own hand. Hannah's prayer ends not in comfort alone, but in vision: the Lord judges all the earth and lifts His chosen.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Samuel stays behind, a child serving before the Lord in Shiloh. Elkanah returns home, and the boy remains—given up as promised, yet not abandoned. The Lord's hand holds him now as surely as Hannah's once did.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Eli's sons are wicked—and they don't know the Lord. This is the root: not merely bad behavior, but a heart unmoved by God's presence. They serve in His house yet are strangers to His character.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The priestly custom was meant to honor the Lord—the fork of three teeth, the portions taken from the sacrifice. Custom itself is not corruption; but when hearts are far from God, even holy rites become tools for plunder.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They seized whatever the fork brought up. No measure, no restraint—taking greedily in the very place where offerings belonged to God. The hands that should have been lifted in worship were clenched in theft.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Even before the fat was burned—before God's portion was honored—they demanded raw meat for themselves. The order itself mattered to God. These men turned the sacrifice inside out, reversing honor to shame.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Give it or I will take it by force." No plea, no deference—only demand backed by strength. This is the fruit of not knowing the Lord: your strength becomes your god, and you use it without mercy or restraint.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Their sin was great because they despised the offering itself—and in it, the God to whom it belonged. Sin is not just wrongdoing; it is contempt for the Holy One. The Lord saw, and it grieved Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Samuel ministered, clothed in the linen ephod—the priest's garment. A child, yet walking before the Lord with reverence. Contrast sharpens truth: in the same place, one youth seeks God's face while others seek their own gain.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hannah's hands keep working—she sews him a robe, small enough for a growing boy. Love doesn't forget even when it has given. Year after year, her needlework carries to Shiloh the message: I remember you; I hold you in my prayers.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Eli blesses them, asking the Lord to grant them more children. It is a generous word—Eli's heart is not yet hardened, and he blesses the one who gave her son. The prayer is answered: the Lord visits Hannah with more sons and daughters.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Three sons and two daughters born to Hannah—the barren woman becomes fruitful. Meanwhile, Samuel grows before the Lord, not just in body but in favor with Him. The Lord remembers her petition, and the family flourishes.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Old Eli hears what his sons have done—the wickedness spreading like a stain through Israel. They even slept with women serving at the tent, mixing greed with lust. Age brings the burden of knowledge when a father learns his children are corrupt.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Why do you do such things?" His rebuke comes late, and his tone carries weariness—he has heard of their deeds from all the people. Shame rises not just from his sins, but that his sins are known throughout Israel.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "No good report"—their actions are public scandal. They make the Lord's people stumble and disobey. A father sees at last that his sons have become stumbling stones in the Lord's house, leading others astray.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sin against God stands apart—no mediator can intercede for it. Yet they don't listen to their father's voice. The heart that will not hear a father cannot hear the Lord either. And Yahweh has hardened them toward their own judgment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Samuel grows in favor with both Yahweh and man. Favor is not favor with all at once, but it flows from a heart turned toward God. The boy who serves faithfully finds himself beloved, and the Lord's hand rests on him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A man of God comes to speak Yahweh's word to Eli. The Lord does not allow corruption to stand without witness. Even old Eli, now helpless to stop his sons, must hear: the Lord remembers every covenant and every breach of it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Chosen from all Israel to be priest, to burn incense and wear the ephod—his house was given all the offerings made by fire. Such privilege, such trust. And they squandered it for meat and lust, forgetting whose house they served.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Why do you kick at my sacrifice?" The image stings: kicking the very offering meant to honor the Lord, honoring sons instead of God, making yourselves fat on what belongs to Him. Contempt wears the face of appetite.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Those who honor me I will honor; those who despise me will be lightly esteemed." This is the law written into all things: honor and dishonor return to their source. The Lord's justice is not grudging—it is the nature of His kingdom.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The arm will be cut off—the strength and offspring of Eli's line. No old man will remain in his house. The sentence is declared: this priestly house, once chosen, now broken. The Lord's judgment is terrible when His honor is mocked.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Eli will see the affliction of God's habitation—and even Israel's wealth will not comfort him. His house will have no old men to carry the name forward. The line ends in shame, and the land's blessing only deepens his loss.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: One might escape the altar's edge, but will waste away—eyes consumed, heart grieving, his children dying young. This is the lingering sorrow the Lord permits: enough mercy to live, enough judgment to know the price of betrayal.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hophni and Phinehas, named here for the first time in judgment: both will die in one day. The sign given now will come to pass—the Lord's word, once spoken, cannot return empty. Eli will know that the prophet spoke truth.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo in this promise: a faithful priest will rise, doing what is in the Lord's heart and mind, walking before the anointed forever. The corrupt line falls; a new priesthood begins. The Lord's purposes are not thwarted by human failure—they are fulfilled through His faithful ones.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Those left will bow for a scrap of silver and bread, begging for priestly office. The high place becomes a place of begging; honor collapses into want. This is what happens when the Lord's house is treated as a thing to own and exploit.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
